stops.note: a sprout or shoot, perhaps of Persian origin
Cato the Elder's De Agri Cultura (c. 160 BC) gives instructions for growing it
folk etymology turned 'sperage' into 'sparrowgrass'; on 20 April 1667 Samuel Pepys bought 'a hundred of sparrowgrass' in Fenchurch Street
the Latin form was restored in polite speech, and 'sparrowgrass' was dismissed as vulgar

current_meaning: a plant whose young shoots are eaten as a vegetable
